newsitem.title: SPAIN: Clinton working on ideas to end Mideast deadlock.
newsitem.headline: Clinton working on ideas to end Mideast deadlock.

text.p: U.S. President Bill Clinton said on Wednesday he was very concerned about the deadlock in the Middle East peace process and was working on ideas to get it moving again.
"It is obvious that we're going to have to see some new specific actions taken in order to get this thing going agaIn," Clinton told a news conference after a two-day NATO summit in Madrid.
"I'm very concerned about what's happening in the peace process. I'm very concerned about the growing tensions between the Palestinians and the Israelis," Clinton said.

"I have been working before I came here to come up with some ideas about how we can start this again... I think it can be done, it is a question of will and risk -- calculated risk -- that's what the peace process in the Middle East has always been about, and we are working on it now."
The Palestinians have refused to continue peace talks with Israel since March when the Jewish state began work on a housing project in traditionally Arab East Jerusalem.
Clinton declined to say what he had in mind, but said it was essential that Palestinian security cooperation with Israel -- which was also broken off in March -- should resume.
